sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: signs and traffic signals
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
Sign meanings are taken from the captions printed beside each sign; the sign pictures themselves are not in the extracted text, so shapes are stated only where the caption names them (octagon, triangle, square) [A01].
The HOV lane caption says the occupancy is as noted on the sign; the example sign on that page shows two or more, so the dossier states the rule as the posted number with two or more as the example [A03].
The safety corridor caption defines corridors by comparison with the statewide crash average and asks drivers to turn on lights; no corridor list is given, so none is stated [A07].
The sample test questions page (physical page twenty-five) is official question text and is not reproduced or paraphrased into facts.
Part C declares dedicated visual surfaces for sign recognition and signal scenarios; official sign and signal images must be sourced separately from the manual text.

corpus_stability.reason: The Oregon Driver Manual is a two-year edition (the front cover names a two-year span and the back cover carries a single form revision code); fees and office details are sent to the DMV website rather than printed, and nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year.
